name: cmd-2-opens-the-second-favourite
description:
The second-favourite chord must open the SECOND favourite tile of the active space, the same way a click on it does, rather than Chromium's select-tab-N on the shared strip.

THE CHORD. It is Cmd+Opt+2, because the plain digits belong to the spaces. What this scenario measures is unchanged: a digit chord resolves a tile slot of the ACTIVE space's grid and opens a cold tile.

The fixture's grid is three tiles in a known order: Blue Favicon Site, Edit Focus, Redirecting Fav. Only the first has a live tab when the window opens, so the second is a cold tile and Cmd+2 has to reopen it - which is the harder half of the click's behaviour and the one a strip-tab binding could never produce. The reading is the sidebar DOM: which tile carries the selected class, by position in the grid. A control read before the key records that neither the second nor the third tile is selected, so the after state cannot be the fixture's own.

The log lines name the route: the chord reached the Atrium action rather than IDC_SELECT_TAB_1, the window resolved slot 2 to tile index 1, and the favourite path opened that URL.

actions.note: ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot

actions.expression: (() => { const f = [...document.querySelectorAll('.fav')]; return 'tiles=' + f.length + ' second=' + f[1].classList.contains('sel') + ' third=' + f[2].classList.contains('sel'); })()
actions.note: THE CONTROL: three tiles, and neither the second nor the third is the active one. Both are cold at startup, so a pass here cannot be the fixture's own state showing through later.

actions.expression: (() => { const f = [...document.querySelectorAll('.fav')]; return 'tiles=' + f.length + ' second=' + f[1].classList.contains('sel') + ' third=' + f[2].classList.contains('sel'); })()
actions.note: The second tile is the selected one now. The grid still has three, so this is a selection moving rather than a redraw.

assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: the second tile was not the active one before the key.

assertions.label: the-chord-reached-the-map
assertions.desc: Cmd+Opt+2 ran the Atrium action. Chromium's select-tab-2 leaves no such line.

assertions.label: the-window-resolved-the-slot
assertions.desc: The digit named the second tile of the active space's grid.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: cold sidebar row opening http://127\.0\.0\.1 \(path len 22\)
assertions.label: the-second-favourite-opened
assertions.desc: The second tile is cold, so the key had to reopen it - the same branch a click takes. The line carries the eTLD (both cold tiles share http://127.0.0.1) and the opened path's length instead of the URL; edit-focus-field.html is 22 characters and redirect-to-lab.html is 21, which is what tells this pair apart post-redaction.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: cold sidebar row opening http://127\.0\.0\.1 \(path len 21\)
assertions.label: not-the-third-tile
assertions.desc: Cmd+2 is the second tile and nothing else. The third is the other cold one (redirect-to-lab.html, path length 21), so it is what an off-by-one would open.
The sidebar draws the SECOND tile as the active one, and the third is untouched.
